Sports injuries can affect athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and even individuals who engage in regular physical activity. While some injuries may seem minor initially, ignoring them can lead to prolonged pain and delayed recovery.

Fracture Treatment Near Jogeshwari — A Complete Patient Guide for Faster Recovery

A fracture, commonly known as a broken bone, can occur due to falls, sports injuries, road accidents, or sudden trauma. While some fractures are obvious and cause severe pain, others may present with swelling, bruising, tenderness, or difficulty moving the affected area. Seeking prompt medical attention is essential to ensure proper healing and prevent complications.

The first step in fracture treatment is an accurate diagnosis, usually through a physical examination and imaging tests such as X-rays. Depending on the type and severity of the fracture, treatment may involve casting, splinting, medication, physiotherapy, or surgery. Following your doctor's instructions carefully is crucial for a smooth recovery.

Patients can support healing by getting adequate rest, maintaining a nutritious diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, and avoiding activities that place stress on the injured bone. Rehabilitation exercises may also be recommended to restore strength, flexibility, and mobility after the fracture begins to heal.

Back Pain in Jogeshwari — When Home Remedies Are Not Enough and a Doctor Is Needed

Back pain is one of the most common health complaints and is often caused by poor posture, muscle strain, prolonged sitting, or heavy lifting. While mild discomfort may improve with rest, stretching, and home remedies, persistent or severe back pain should not be ignored.

If your back pain lasts for more than a few weeks, keeps returning, interferes with daily activities, or becomes worse over time, it may indicate an underlying condition that requires medical attention. Symptoms such as pain radiating down the legs, numbness, tingling, weakness, or difficulty standing and walking should be evaluated by a specialist as soon as possible.

Common causes of chronic back pain include slipped discs, arthritis, spinal degeneration, nerve compression, and sports or workplace injuries. Early diagnosis can help prevent complications and improve recovery outcomes.

ECG Test in Jogeshwari — What It Detects and Why Doctors Recommend It

An Electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most commonly recommended heart tests and plays an important role in evaluating heart health. The test records the electrical activity of the heart and helps doctors identify potential cardiac problems quickly and non-invasively.

Doctors may recommend an ECG if a patient experiences symptoms such as chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness, or unexplained fatigue. The test can help detect irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias), signs of a previous heart attack, reduced blood flow to the heart, and other abnormalities that may affect heart function.

An ECG is also commonly used as part of routine health screenings for individuals with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a family history of heart disease. Early detection of heart-related issues allows for timely treatment and better long-term outcomes.

If you are experiencing heart-related symptoms or have risk factors for cardiovascular disease, consulting a cardiologist in Jogeshwari can help determine whether an ECG is required. Heart Checkup in Jogeshwari Who Needs It and How Often Should You Go?

Many heart conditions develop gradually and may not show clear symptoms in their early stages. That's why regular heart screenings are important, especially for individuals with risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, smoking, or a family history of heart disease. Consulting a cardiologist in Jogeshwari can help detect potential heart problems before they become serious.

A heart checkup is also recommended for people experiencing chest discomfort, shortness of breath, dizziness, heart palpitations, or unexplained fatigue. Adults over the age of 40 should consider periodic cardiac evaluations, while those with existing health conditions may require more frequent monitoring based on their doctor's advice.

Routine tests such as blood pressure monitoring, ECG, cholesterol screening, and other cardiac assessments can provide valuable insights into your heart health. Early diagnosis allows for timely treatment and lifestyle modifications that may help prevent future complications.

Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.

featured_reviews.review_text:
To,
The Management,
Sanjeevni Hospital, Andheri East

Subject: Serious Concerns Regarding Hospital Facilities, Staff Management & Patient Care

I am writing this feedback with deep disappointment regarding the overall experience and facilities provided during our patient’s admission for knee replacement surgery at your hospital.

There appears to be only 1 sister/nurse and 1 housekeeping staff managing 3 floors. In case of emergencies, even after ringing the bell repeatedly, the staff arrives extremely late — sometimes after nearly an hour. In a medical emergency, such delays can become life-threatening. The management seriously needs to address this issue immediately and appoint more staff for proper patient care and safety.

The cleanliness and maintenance standards of the hospital are also extremely poor. Rooms and patient areas were not cleaned properly, and hygiene was highly disappointing.

Food service was another major concern:
- Morning breakfast was either delayed or sometimes not provided at all.
- The quality of food served was extremely poor and difficult even for patients to consume.

The discharge process was unnecessarily lengthy and unorganized:
- Even after the doctor approved discharge, it took around 1.5 to 2 hours just to send the file to the billing counter.
- Thereafter, another 2 to 3 hours were wasted in completing billing and discharge formalities.
- Overall, discharge took almost 4 to 5 hours, causing unnecessary inconvenience to patients and their families.

The hospital also urgently requires:
- Better management systems
- More nursing and housekeeping staff
- Proper stretcher lifts
- Better food and qualified cooks
- Improved hygiene and room maintenance

Another highly disappointing aspect was that the doctor who performed the knee replacement surgery did not visit the patient even once during the entire 4-day admission period after surgery.

Additionally, hospital clothes provided to patients were not changed regularly. When requested for fresh clothes, the staff kept giving excuses such as “it is in laundry.” This is unacceptable for admitted patients who require proper hygiene and care.

Overall, the experience was extremely disappointing and far below expected healthcare standards. The hospital management seriously needs to improve patient care, staffing, cleanliness, food quality, emergency response time, and administrative efficiency.

We hope this feedback is taken seriously and immediate corrective measures are implemented so that future patients and their families do not face similar difficulties.

Regards,
Damyanti Gala

owner_posts.post_text: In a world that moves fast, yoga reminds us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with ourselves.

A patient came to us after nearly three months of continuous fever following a knee replacement surgery. During this period, she had consulted multiple doctors across cities and was treated for common infections like typhoid, malaria and dengue. Despite repeated tests and treatments, the fever persisted, along with joint pain, mouth ulcers and extreme fatigue — without a clear diagnosis.

At SRV Hospitals, under the care of Dr. Avilash Tiwari @dr.avilash_tiwari, the approach shifted from treating symptoms to understanding the full cause. A structured evaluation for long-standing fever was initiated, looking beyond routine infections and considering inflammatory and immune-related conditions.

Advanced testing revealed two key findings. One was a mild, uncommon form of leptospirosis that does not present with the typical severe symptoms and often goes unnoticed. More importantly, investigations confirmed an autoimmune condition called Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), where the immune system becomes overactive and causes ongoing inflammation — leading to persistent fever and joint symptoms.

Our second DEEP session on "Approach to Patient with Stroke" continued Phase 1 with sharp clinical decision-making insights and case-based learning.
Key highlights included:
▪️ NIHSS scoring & interpretation
▪️ Thrombolysis — the 4.5-hour window

SBS Hospital claims to provide “world-class medical services at an affordable price,” but our experience was far from this promise.
My mother-in-law was admitted twice (9–17 December and 20–23 January) under Dr. Ankita Chauhan for severe UTI and electrolyte imbalance. While the doctor was competent, the hospital administration and billing practices were extremely disappointing.
During the first admission, Post depositing ₹20,000, the hospital bill reached ₹89,000. Medicines and IVs were billed separately (≈₹50,000) with only a 10% discount, pathology tests were outsourced at high rates, and daily payments were demanded from both hospital and pharmacy, treating relatives like potential defaulters.
During the second admission, patient comfort was ignored—AC switched off, no fan, and repeated requests to nurses and resident doctors were ignored for two days, until strong protest.
On discharge day (23 January), despite the doctor clearly instructing that we should not be charged for the day, the receptionist—while remaining outwardly calm and polite—kept repeatedly pressuring and subtly threatening us with additional charges if payment was delayed. Even after explaining our situation, reminders continued (“it’s already 3 p.m.”, “you’ll be charged”, "Its already 4:30"), creating unnecessary stress.  We had informed her we did not have the money and my Sis in law will make the payment. (She already has 2 patients to take care of 1 is a dialysis patient and other is a parkinsons patient.) That was the breaking point.  We were not going to abscond.  When me and my husband finally raised our voice, she said, “Ma’am, why are you shouting? And told my husband that There are cameras.”  We were angry only when she showed no empathy, patience and was repeatedly after us.    Only after admin intervention did the situation de-escalate.
Speaking softly does not equal empathy. The hospital staff needs serious training in humanity and patient/relative handling, not just protocols.
Please do not blindly trust online ratings—I personally witnessed reception staff helping non–tech-savvy relatives submit reviews.
The only saving grace of this hospital is Dr. Ankita Chauhan and the Mavshis.

Hospital bill: ₹43,000 (after ₹1,300 discount,  1200 for the oxymeter and 100 to round off the amount)

The hospital is exceptionally well-maintained, with clean surroundings and efficient systems that make the entire process—from admission to daily check-ins—smooth and reassuring. The medical team is knowledgeable and attentive, taking time to explain treatment plans clearly, and the nursing staff consistently shows patience, warmth and professionalism.

A special mention goes to Chef Puran, whose dedication genuinely stood out. He was extremely accommodating with the dietary needs of the attendant, ensuring bland meals were prepared exactly as requested. He also took the effort to personally visit the room to confirm that everything was suitable and comfortable, which was incredibly thoughtful and speaks volumes about the hospital’s commitment to patient and caregiver wellbeing.

I would also like to acknowledge the Floor Manager, Mr. Sajeed Sheikh, who was consistently attentive and reassuring. He took the time to personally check on the patient, ensuring comfort and addressing any concerns with warmth and professionalism.

Additionally, as we were leaving the hospital, staff member Sunita Harijan and Security personnel Dhanshree called us to let us know that a phone charger had been left behind. Since we were just at the gate, we went back and collected it. I’m very grateful for their honesty and prompt action.

featured_reviews.name: Ashok
featured_reviews.review_text: I am extremely thankful to Dr. Gautam Goel sir for my successful surgery. and staff for their support. The Gleneagles Hospital maintained excellent hygiene across room, bed sheet and patient clothing. Diet food was provided on time and the medical team ensured continuous monitoring with regular check-ups. Additionally... the insurance process with Care Health Insurance was handled seamlessly with smooth and hassle-free paperwork. Truly appreciate the overall care and management.

It truely meant a lot to us.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Karan Admane
featured_reviews.review_text: The OPD staff at Gleneagles Hospital are truly exceptional! Their professionalism and teamwork make my job as a doctor much easier. Kudos to the entire team!

featured_reviews.name: santosh kedare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very good experience at Gleneagles Hospitals. The Nephrology team provided excellent care and support throughout my treatment.
I would like to sincerely thank Dr. Bharat Shah, Dr. Prashant Rajput, Dr. Shruti Tapiawala, Dr. Hepal Vora, and Dr. Zaheer Virani for their expertise, kindness, and dedication.
Special appreciation also goes to the surgical team, including Dr. Pradeep Rao, Dr. Jitendra Jagtap, Dr. Lokesh Sinha, and Dr. Mrudula Kuchekar, as well as the anaesthesia team for their professionalism and excellent care.
The doctors, nurses, and support staff were compassionate, attentive, and always willing to help. I am grateful for the quality treatment and care I received. I highly recommend Gleneagles Hospital to anyone seeking expert medical care.
